chunk_findings.detail: `GitProbes.__init__` defaults `min_git` to `"2.38"`, but this change exists so conflict detection uses the probe's 2.43 `merge-tree` gate and scratch-merge fallback (the new module docstring says an older git must not come back as "could not tell" for a version reason). Any still-valid one-arg call `GitProbes(repo)` — the previous signature — forwards `min_git="2.38"`. On git 2.40, `probe.run` then treats `--write-tree` as allowed, hits the pre-2.43 exit-code bug, and returns unavailable, so `conflicts` yields `None` instead of the scratch-merge bool. Only `api/metrics.py` passes `cfg.locks.probe_merge_tree_min_git`; the class default reintroduces the drift the wrapper was meant to remove. The new test always constructs `GitProbes(..., min_git="2.43")` and stubs `probe_run`, so it never sees this input.

chunk_findings.detail: `p = GitProbes(tmp_path, 30, "2.38")` explicitly sets `min_git` back to the old unsafe threshold. `probe.run` treats `min_git="2.38"` as permission to use `git merge-tree --write-tree` on Git 2.38 and later, but versions 2.38–2.42 have the pre-2.43 exit-code defect the probe’s new threshold exists to avoid; on those versions the probe returns `UNAVAILABLE`, so `p.conflicts(main, side) is True` and `p.conflicts(base, side) is False` in this same test receive `None` and fail. The safe default/omitted `min_git` would route Git 2.38–2.42 through the scratch-merge fallback instead, so this changed line should not force `"2.38"`.

chunk_findings.detail: The only real-git check of `GitProbes.conflicts` was updated to `GitProbes(tmp_path, 30, "2.38")` and then asserts `p.conflicts(main, side) is True` on branches that actually conflict. `min_git="2.38"` is the gate this change was written to stop using: on git 2.40 (at least 2.38, before 2.43) `probe.run` treats `merge-tree --write-tree` as allowed, hits the pre-2.43 exit-code bug, and returns unavailable, so `conflicts` returns `None` and the assertion fails (or, if that bug reports exit 0, returns `False` for a real conflict). The new module docstring promises an older git falls back to a scratch merge and is never "could not tell" for a version reason; this call opts the regression guard back into the broken threshold instead of `probe_merge_tree_min_git` / `"2.43"`.

chunk_findings.detail: `module_names` never refuses a duplicated module name, so the advertised multi-path scan can hide a section instead of raising. `pkgutil.iter_modules` walks every entry of `package.__path__` and the comprehension only sorts; given `__path__ == [dir_a, dir_b]` where both contain `agent.py`, it returns `("agent", "agent", ...)`. `SECTION_MODULES` then calls `import_module` twice, the second hit is the `sys.modules` cache, and the other file never runs, so `@declare` never sees the clash. The new test only re-invokes `_docs.declare` on an already-registered name; it never feeds the scan two path entries with the same filename, so this input stays green.

chunk_findings.detail: The throwaway import mutates process-global registry state and never rolls it back. `importlib.import_module("ddflow.config_sections.zzz_throwaway")` executes `@declare("zzz_throwaway")`, which inserts into `_docs.SECTION_CLASSES` and leaves `sys.modules["ddflow.config_sections.zzz_throwaway"]` populated. `monkeypatch` restores `__path__` only. After this test, any later test that builds `Config`, the knob manifest, or the golden section set from `SECTION_CLASSES` observes `zzz_throwaway` (default `zzz_count=1`) even though that module is not in the real package. There is no `finally` that pops the key or drops the cached module.

chunk_findings.detail: The byte-identity checks cannot fail and do not lock the seam this change claims to prove. `init_before` / `core_before` are read, then the test only extends `__path__`, calls `module_names`, and `import_module`s a throwaway module; none of those writes `config/__init__.py` or `config/_core.py`, so the asserts pass even if those files still hold a hand-kept section list that a real new `[section]` must edit. It also never reloads the package, so `SECTION_NAMES` / `SECTION_MODULES` (the tuples the rest of config actually consumes, fixed at import) are not shown to include `zzz_throwaway`, and `Config` fields, the docs table, the knob manifest, and the golden surface are never generated from the discovered module. `test_a_duplicate_section_name_is_refused` only re-invokes `_docs.declare` on an already-registered name; it does not feed the scan two modules that declare the same section.

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed seam hole is still open. `test_a_new_section_module_is_discovered_without_editing_shared_files` still only extends `__path__`, scans names, and imports a throwaway module; it never reloads `ddflow.config` or builds `Config`, so with `extra_sections/zzz_throwaway.py` present the byte asserts at lines 88-89 compare each file to itself and pass even if `config/__init__.py` and `config/_core.py` still contain a hand-kept section list. The new `test_config_fields_classes_and_knob_manifest_come_from_the_registry` does not close that. `set(C._SECTION_CLASS_BY_NAME) == {c.__name__ for c in ...}` ignores the dict values, so `{name: None for name in class names}` passes, and the knob check is `if f in DECLARED_IN.values() or key in KNOB_DOCS: assert key in KNOB_DOCS`, which is exactly `if f in DECLARED_IN.values()`. A field such as `zzz_count` whose name is not a `DECLARED_IN` value, with `section.zzz_count` absent from a hand-kept `KNOB_DOCS`, skips the assert. A static list kept equal to today's registry therefore still passes both tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The test `test_a_new_section_module_is_discovered_without_editing_shared_files` monkeypatches `ddflow.config_sections.__path__` *after* `ddflow.config` and `ddflow.config_sections` have already been imported and their module-level execution has run. At that point, `SECTION_NAMES` and `SECTION_MODULES` in `ddflow.config_sections` have already been evaluated and will not contain `zzz_throwaway`. Therefore, when the test asserts `"zzz_throwaway" in CS.module_names(CS)`, `CS.module_names(CS)` scans `CS`, whose `__path__` is still the original package directory (not `tmp_path / "extra_sections"`), so `"zzz_throwaway"` is never in `CS.module_names(CS)` and the test fails or produces a false outcome (or `importlib.import_module` succeeds only because it imports an arbitrary path that was never integrated into the package's `SECTION_NAMES` or `SECTION_MODULES`).
